From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: AcmeHealth - Private/VPC post-call recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — great conversation and appreciate the clarity on your constraints. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Key goals you shared:
- Host PHI-sensitive inference workloads in an isolated environment (no egress to public internet).
- Data residency: all model inputs/outputs must remain in US-East.
- Low-latency inference for clinician-facing workflows (95th p99 target under 300ms for short prompts).
- Strong audit logging and key management integration with your existing KMS/HSM.

Primary pain points:
- Current vendor solutions either expose network egress or require heavy engineering to air-gap.
- Procurement needs clear SOW and customer-managed network design before legal signs off.
- Ops needs a simple upgrade path for patches and model rollouts without opening outbound ports.

Technical constraints you called out:
- All traffic must flow over a customer-managed VPC peering or direct connect; no public IPs allowed for inference nodes.
- Strict egress policy: only explicit outbound to your update server via a proxy allowed (we discussed a pull-based package delivery).
- Requirement for a fully air-gapped on-prem option if cloud connectivity is not approved by compliance.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed networking and optional on-prem air-gap package.
- Integrations for KMS/HSM and audit-log forwarding (we can ship logs to your SIEM over approved channels).
- A solutions-engineering-led technical deep-dive to validate ports, proxy configs, and package delivery approach.

Attachments included: redwood-private-vpc-architecture.pdf (high-level architecture), soc2-overview.pdf (SOC2 artifact summary).

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/ops + our Solutions Engineer (Dev) — available Thu 11 Feb 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 12 Feb 13:00–14:00 PT.
2) You share a redacted network diagram and procurement timeline (Karen) — we can do an initial SOW draft after the deep-dive.
3) If an air-gap is required, we'll prepare a separate runbook and estimate for packaging and on-prem install (timeline and scoping).

Questions for you (short):
- Confirm whether updates can be delivered via an approved internal proxy (pull model) or if the environment must be completely isolated with manual updates.
- Any specific port-blocking policies we should know (e.g., outbound only to 443 via proxy, no DNS allowed)?

Next action: Jordan — can you confirm attendee list for the technical deep-dive and which of the two time options looks best?

Thanks again,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0142

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. Happy to confirm a few items from our side: 

- Residency: must be US-East (we host primary EHR in us-east-1).
- Updates: preferred model is pull-based via our internal proxy (we do not allow arbitrary outbound to the internet). We can expose an internal update endpoint (reachable only over the peered VPC).
- Ports: outbound 443 via proxy is OK; DNS must be resolved internally (no external DNS queries).
- Air-gap: compliance says we need the option to run fully air-gapped on-prem for certain environments (pilot must support this).

I attached a very high-level network sketch (acme_network_sketch.png) — redacted. 

For the technical deep-dive, Thu 11 Feb 10:00–11:00 PT works for our infra leads (I will invite: Priya Sinha (infra lead), Omar Watts (network), and Karen Li (procurement)).

We'd like to see a short checklist from your solutions engineer on what we'll need to open/enable on our side to validate the deployment during the deep-dive. Also please include an initial SOW outline post-call.

Jordan
Director of Engineering | AcmeHealth
j.king@acmehealth.com | +1 212-555-0199

Thanks for the context — quick technical notes from my side ahead of the deep-dive: 

- We can support two deployment modes: 1) Customer VPC (dedicated subnets, private IPs, no public IPs) with peering/direct-connect and 2) On-prem air-gapped package. Both support KMS integration and audit-log forwarding.
- For the pull-based update flow: we build the package signed and expose an update artifact endpoint that can be pulled over HTTPS via your proxy. We can also support signed USB/image delivery when fully air-gapped.
- Ports: our runtime only needs outbound HTTPS to the update endpoint during patch operations (otherwise none). For monitoring/log forwarding we can push to an internal syslog endpoint or forward logs over an approved secure channel.
- During the deep-dive we'll need: a redacted network diagram (thanks Jordan), list of proxy credentials/paths to validate pull, and the IP ranges or peering details for routing.

I can run the deep-dive and bring an infra engineer (Priyom) to map the exact port and routing requirements. We'll prepare a short checklist and send it before the meeting.
